findings.title: Light-theme color changed for embedded post author link
findings.body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` passes 70% as the light-theme value instead of 30%, so author links in embedded posts become noticeably lighter/lower-contrast on light themes. The PR's stated intent is only to add a dark-theme branch; the light value should stay 30%.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; the new first argument to `dark-light-choose` is 50%, lightening the name text on light themes and also removing the previous visual distinction between `.name` (30%) and `.title` (50%). The light-theme value should remain 30%.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same regression as the desktop file: `.group-member-info .name` used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now passes 50% as the light-theme argument, changing the light theme rendering and collapsing the contrast difference with `.title`.

findings.title: custom-message-length light/dark values swapped relative to original
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the change passes 30% for the light theme and 70% for `$secondary` in the dark theme. This makes the mobile hint text much darker on light themes and inconsistent with the equivalent desktop rule (`70%` light / `30%` dark). The light argument should be 70%.

findings.title: topic-map h3 light value changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and now passes 50% for the light theme, lightening the topic map heading on light themes (desktop keeps 20%). The light-theme argument should stay 20% to preserve existing appearance and desktop/mobile parity.
